brief: Goldman's Ben Snider (US Weekly Kickstart) argues rising cost-of-capital pressure has made the equity market downgrade growth expectations: Goldman's Cyclicals vs Defensives pair fell 6% in two weeks, the 10Y yield dropped over 20bp after rising 100bp+, and USD high-yield spreads widened over 20bp, concentrated in AI issuers. AI-exposed stocks (neoclouds -24.8% on the week, semis down eight straight sessions, the momentum factor -14.5%) led the selloff as hedge funds sold the AI stock they had bought since January 2025 and net leverage fell to a five-year-low 43.7%. Goldman's baseline is S&P EPS growth slowing from 36% this year to 11% in 2027, since AI capex drives roughly half of current EPS growth and turns earnings-negative by 2028. Historically decelerating growth favors the momentum factor, but Goldman says breadth near dot-com extremes means momentum reverses regardless of direction. Snider recommends going long "catch-up" (consumer-discretionary laggards, needing oil near $75) hedged with "catch-down" (defensive healthcare/staples), short momentum, while keeping GS's 8,000/8,700 S&P targets. The article's own view leans toward the catch-down resolving first.
